question: Under the Bolam standard, a surgeon is negligent if their management differs from what a responsible body of surgeons would have done, even if alternative approaches exist.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: The Bolam standard does hold that acting in a way no responsible body of practitioners would endorse constitutes negligence. It is not enough that one alternative approach exists; the key is whether the chosen approach would be accepted by a responsible body of peers.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The Bolam test defines negligence by comparison to a responsible body of peers. Deviation from accepted practice — not the mere existence of alternatives — establishes the breach of duty.
